units.zh: 梁書卷第四十六 列傳第四十
units.en: Book of Liang, Volume 46, Biography 40
units.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 46, Biography 40

units.zh: 胡僧祐 徐文盛 杜崱 兄岸 弟幼安 兄子龕 陰子春
units.en: Hu Sengyou; Xu Wensheng; Du Ze; Du An; Du You'an; Du Kan; Yin Zichun
units.literal: Hu Sengyou, Xu Wensheng, Du Ze, elder brother An, younger brother You'an, elder brother's son Kan, Yin Zichun

units.zh: 胡僧祐字願果，南陽冠軍人。
units.en: Hu Sengyou, styled Yuanguo, came from Guanjun in Nanyang.
units.literal: Hu Sengyou, styled Yuanguo, came from Guanjun in Nanyang.

units.zh: 少勇決，有武幹。
units.en: In youth he was brave and resolute and had military ability.
units.literal: In youth he was brave and resolute and had military ability.

units.zh: 仕魏至銀青光祿大夫，以大通二年歸國，頻上封事，高祖器之，拜假節、超武將軍、文德主帥，使戍項城。
units.en: He served Wei, reaching Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon. In Datong 2 he returned to Liang and repeatedly submitted sealed memorials. Gaozu valued him and appointed him acting staff-bearer, General Who Surpasses Martial Might, and commander of the Wende guard, sending him to garrison Xiangcheng.
units.literal: He served Wei, reaching Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon. In Datong 2 he returned to Liang and repeatedly submitted sealed memorials. Gaozu valued him and appointed him acting staff-bearer, General Who Surpasses Martial Might, and commander of the Wende guard, sending him to garrison Xiangcheng.

units.zh: 城陷，復沒于魏。
units.en: When the city fell, he was again lost to Wei.
units.literal: When the city fell, he was again lost to Wei.

units.zh: 中大通元年，陳慶之送魏北海王元顥入洛陽，僧祐又得還國，除南天水、天門二郡太守，有善政。
units.en: In Zhongdatong 1, when Chen Qingzhi escorted Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai of Wei, into Luoyang, Sengyou again managed to return to Liang. He was appointed administrator of South Tianshui and Tianmen commanderies and governed well.
units.literal: In Zhongdatong 1, when Chen Qingzhi escorted Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai of Wei, into Luoyang, Sengyou again managed to return to Liang. He was appointed administrator of South Tianshui and Tianmen commanderies and governed well.

units.zh: 性好讀書，不解緝綴。
units.en: By nature he loved reading, but he did not understand literary composition.
units.literal: By nature he loved reading, but he did not understand literary composition.

units.zh: 然每在公宴，必強賦詩，文辭鄙俚，多被嘲謔，僧祐怡然自若，謂己實工，矜伐愈甚。
units.en: Yet whenever he attended public banquets, he always forced himself to compose poems. His wording was crude and rustic, and he was often mocked, but Sengyou remained perfectly at ease, believed himself truly skilled, and boasted all the more.
units.literal: Yet whenever he attended public banquets, he always forced himself to compose poems. His wording was crude and rustic, and he was often mocked, but Sengyou remained perfectly at ease, believed himself truly skilled, and boasted all the more.

units.zh: 晚事世祖，爲鎮西錄事參軍。
units.en: Later he served Shizu as recorder on the Pacifying West staff.
units.literal: In his later years he served Emperor Shizu as staff recorder in the Pacifying West headquarters.

units.zh: 侯景亂，西沮蠻反，世祖令僧祐討之，使盡誅其渠帥，僧祐諫，忤旨下獄。
units.en: When Hou Jing rebelled the Western Ju rose; Shizu ordered Sengyou to put them down and kill every chieftain; Sengyou remonstrated, offended the throne, and was jailed.
units.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, the Western Ju barbarians revolted; Shizu ordered Sengyou to suppress them and to execute all their chieftains; Sengyou remonstrated and, defying the edict, was thrown into prison.

units.zh: 大寶二年，侯景寇荊陝，圍王僧辯于巴陵，世祖乃引僧祐於獄，拜爲假節、武猛將軍，封新市縣侯，令赴援。
units.en: In Great Treasure year two Hou Jing raided Jing-Shan and besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling; Shizu freed Sengyou, made him acting staff bearer, General of Martial Ferocity, and Marquis of Xinshi, and sent him to relieve the siege.
units.literal: In the second year of Great Treasure, when Hou Jing raided Jing and Shan and besieged Wang Sengbian at Baling, Shizu brought Sengyou out of prison, made him acting bearer of the staff, General of Martial Ferocity, and Marquis of Xinshi county, and ordered him to relieve the siege.

units.zh: 僧祐將發，謂其子曰：「汝可開兩門，一門擬朱，一門擬白。
units.en: As he was about to march he told his son, "Prepare two gates—one for red, one for white.
units.literal: As Sengyou was about to set out he told his son: "You may prepare two gates—one gate for red, one gate for white.

units.zh: 吉則由朱門，凶則由白門。
units.en: If I win, come in by the red gate; if I lose, by the white.
units.literal: If fortune comes, enter by the red gate; if misfortune, by the white gate.

units.zh: 吾不捷不歸也。」
units.en: I will not come home unless I win."
units.literal: I shall not return unless victorious."

units.zh: 世祖聞而壯之。
units.en: Shizu heard and was stirred.
units.literal: When Shizu heard this he admired his spirit.

units.zh: 至楊浦，景遣其將任約率銳卒五千，據白塉，遙以待之。
units.en: At Yangpu, Jing sent Ren Yue with five thousand elites to hold White Embankment and wait for him.
units.literal: Reaching Yangpu, Jing sent his general Ren Yue with five thousand crack troops to hold White Embankment, watching for him from afar.

units.zh: 僧祐由別路西上，約謂畏己而退，急追之，及於南安芊口，呼僧祐曰：「吳兒，何爲不早降？
units.en: Sengyou took a side road west; Yue thought he had fled in fear and chased hard; at Nan'an Qian Ford he shouted to Sengyou, "Wu whelp—why not surrender now?
units.literal: Sengyou took a bypath westward; Yue thought he had feared him and retreated, and pursued urgently; at Nan'an Qian Ford he called to Sengyou: "Wu boy—why do you not surrender early?

units.zh: 走何處去。」
units.en: Where can you run?"
units.literal: Where will you run?"

units.zh: 僧祐不與之言，潛引卻，至赤砂亭，會陸法和至，乃與幷軍擊約，大破之，擒約送于江陵。
units.en: Sengyou would not answer but quietly withdrew; at Red Sand Pavilion Lu Fahe came up, and together they attacked Yue, broke him utterly, captured him, and sent him to Jiangling.
units.literal: Sengyou did not speak with him but secretly drew back; at Red Sand Pavilion layman Lu Fahe arrived, and together they joined armies and struck Yue, routing him greatly; they captured Yue and sent him to Jiangling.

units.zh: 侯景聞之遂遁。
units.en: Hou Jing heard and fled.
units.literal: When Hou Jing heard of it he fled.

units.zh: 世祖以僧祐爲侍中、領軍將軍，徵還荊州。
units.en: Shizu made him palace attendant and commanding general and recalled him to Jingzhou.
units.literal: Shizu made Sengyou palace attendant and General Who Commands the Army, and summoned him back to Jingzhou.

units.zh: 承聖二年，進爲車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，餘悉如故。
units.en: In Chengsheng year two he was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opening-the-Fortress with Three Staffs Equals; the rest unchanged.
units.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Opening-the-Fortress with Three Staffs Equals, all else unchanged.

units.zh: 西魏寇至，以僧祐爲都督城東諸軍事。
units.en: When Western Wei attacked, Shizu made him commander east of the city.
units.literal: When Western Wei raided, Shizu made Sengyou commander of military affairs east of the city.

units.zh: 魏軍四面起攻，百道齊舉，僧祐親當矢石，晝夜督戰，獎勵將士，明於賞罰，衆皆感之，咸爲致死，所向摧殄，賊莫敢前。
units.en: Wei forces assaulted from every side, a hundred lines at once; Sengyou took arrows and stones himself, fighting day and night, clear in rewards and punishments—the men were stirred and died where they stood; nothing could stand before him; the enemy dared not come forward.
units.literal: Wei armies attacked from all four sides, a hundred routes rising together; Sengyou himself met arrows and stones, supervising battle day and night, rewarding soldiers, clear in reward and punishment—all were moved and fought to the death; wherever he turned he crushed and destroyed; the bandits dared not advance.

units.zh: 俄而中流矢卒，時年六十三。
units.en: Soon he was hit by a stray arrow and died at sixty-three.
units.literal: Before long he was struck by a stray arrow and died, aged sixty-three.

units.zh: 世祖聞之，馳往臨哭。
units.en: Shizu heard and rushed to mourn over the body.
units.literal: When Shizu heard, he raced to attend and weep over the corpse.

units.zh: 於是內外惶駭，城遂陷。
units.en: Inside and outside panicked, and the city fell.
units.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were terrified and alarmed, and the city fell.

units.zh: 徐文盛，字道茂，彭城人也。
units.en: Xu Wensheng, styled Daomao, was from Pengcheng.
units.literal: Xu Wensheng, styled Daomao, was a man of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 世仕魏爲將。
units.en: His family had served Wei as generals for generations.
units.literal: For generations his family served Wei as generals.

units.zh: 父慶之，天監初，率千餘人自北歸款，未至道卒。
units.en: His father Qingzhi, early in Heavenly Surveillance, led over a thousand men south to defect but died on the way.
units.literal: His father Qingzhi, at the beginning of Heavenly Surveillance, led more than a thousand men to surrender from the north but died on the road before arriving.

units.zh: 文盛仍統其衆，稍立功績，高祖甚優寵之。
units.en: Wensheng took over the troops, won merit step by step, and Gaozu favored him greatly.
units.literal: Wensheng then took command of his force, gradually achieved merit, and Gaozu favored him exceedingly.

units.zh: 大同末，以爲持節、督寧州刺史。
units.en: At the end of Great Unity he became staff bearer and inspector of Ning.
units.literal: At the end of Great Unity he was made bearer of the staff and inspector of Ning prefecture.

units.zh: 先是，州在僻遠，所管羣蠻不識教義，貪欲財賄，劫篡相尋，前後刺史莫能制。
units.en: The prefecture was remote; the tribes knew no law, only greed and raiding—no earlier governor had controlled them.
units.literal: Earlier the prefecture lay in remote borderland; the tribal barbarians it governed knew no civil teaching, coveted bribes and goods, and plundered one another in succession—no former inspector could control them.

units.zh: 文盛推心撫慰，示以威德，夷獠感之，風俗遂改。
units.en: Wensheng won them with sincerity and awed them with strength; the tribes were moved and manners changed.
units.literal: Wensheng opened his heart to soothe them, showed them might and virtue; the Yi and Liao were moved, and custom was reformed.

units.zh: 太清二年，聞國難，乃召募得數萬人來赴。
units.en: In Supreme Clarity year two, hearing the capital was in peril, he raised tens of thousands and marched east.
units.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity, hearing of the state's calamity, he mustered and recruited several tens of thousands to come to the relief.

units.zh: 世祖嘉之，以爲持節、散騎常侍、左衛將軍、督梁、南秦、沙、東益、巴、北巴六州諸軍事、仁威將軍、秦州刺史，授以東討之略。
units.en: Shizu praised him and made him staff bearer, palace attendant, Left Guard general, commander of six prefectures' forces, General of Benevolent Might, and Qin inspector, with the eastern campaign plan.
units.literal: Shizu praised this and made him bearer of the staff, regular palace attendant, Left Guard general, commander of military affairs in Liang, South Qin, Sha, East Yi, Ba, and North Ba—six prefectures—General of Benevolent Might, and inspector of Qin prefecture, entrusting him with the eastern campaign plan.

units.zh: 於是文盛督衆軍東下，至武昌，遇侯景將任約，遂與相持。
units.en: Wensheng led his host east; at Wuchang he met Ren Yue and stood locked.
units.literal: Thereupon Wensheng led the armies east; reaching Wuchang he met Hou Jing's general Ren Yue and locked in stalemate.

units.zh: 久之，世祖又命護軍將軍尹悅、平東將軍杜幼安、巴州刺史王珣等會之，並受文盛節度。
units.en: After long delay Shizu sent Yin Yue, Du You'an, Wang Xun, and others to join him, all under Wensheng.
units.literal: After a long while Shizu again ordered Protector of the Army Yin Yue, Pacifying East general Du You'an, Ba prefecture governor Wang Xun and others to join him, all under Wensheng's command.

units.zh: 擊任約於貝磯，約大敗，退保西陽。
units.en: They fought Ren Yue at Shell Ford; Yue was routed and fell back on Xiyang.
units.literal: They struck Ren Yue at Shell Ford; Yue was greatly defeated and withdrew to hold Xiyang.

units.zh: 文盛進據蘆洲，又與相持。
units.en: Wensheng took Reed Islet and faced him again.
units.literal: Wensheng advanced and held Reed Islet, again in stalemate.

units.zh: 侯景聞之，乃率大衆西上援約，至西陽。
units.en: Hou Jing heard and led a great force west to save Yue, reaching Xiyang.
units.literal: When Hou Jing heard, he led a great host west to relieve Yue, reaching Xiyang.

units.zh: 文盛不敢戰。
units.en: Wensheng would not give battle.
units.literal: Wensheng did not dare fight.

units.zh: 諸將咸曰：「景水軍輕進，又甚饑疲，可因此擊之，必大捷。」
units.en: The generals said, "Jing's fleet came fast and is starving—we can strike now and win a great victory."
units.literal: The generals all said: "Jing's river army advanced lightly and is very hungry and weary—we can strike now and surely win a great victory."

units.zh: 文盛不許。
units.en: Wensheng refused.
units.literal: Wensheng did not permit it.

units.zh: 文盛妻石氏，先在建鄴，至是，景載以還之。
units.en: Wensheng's wife Lady Shi had been in Jiankang; Jing now sent her back to him.
units.literal: Wensheng's wife the Lady Shi had been in Jiankang; at this time Jing conveyed her back to him.

units.zh: 文盛深德景，遂密通信使，都無戰心，衆咸憤怨。
units.en: Wensheng felt beholden to Jing and began secret correspondence; he would not fight—the army seethed with anger.
units.literal: Wensheng felt deep obligation to Jing and then secretly exchanged envoys; he had no will to fight at all—the host was furious and resentful.

units.zh: 杜幼安、守簉等乃率所領獨進，與景戰，大破之，獲其舟艦以歸。
units.en: Du You'an, Shouzao, and others led their men out alone, fought Jing, smashed him, and brought back his ships.
units.literal: Du You'an, the garrison officer Shouzao and others then led their detachments forward alone, fought Jing, and routed him greatly, capturing his boats and returning.

units.zh: 會景密遣騎從間道襲陷郢州，軍中兇懼，遂大潰。
units.en: Then Jing sent cavalry by a hidden road, took E prefecture, and the army collapsed in terror.
units.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent cavalry by a hidden path to raid and seize E prefecture; the army was panic-stricken and utterly routed.

units.zh: 文盛奔還荊州，世祖仍以爲城北面都督。
units.en: Wensheng fled to Jingzhou; Shizu still made him commander of the north wall.
units.literal: Wensheng fled back to Jingzhou; Shizu still made him commander of the north face of the city.

units.zh: 又聚贓汚甚多，世祖大怒，下令責之，數其十罪，除其官爵。
units.en: He had also piled up loot; Shizu raged, rebuked him, listed ten crimes, and stripped his titles.
units.literal: He had also amassed much corrupt booty; Shizu was greatly angered, issued orders to reproach him, counted his ten crimes, and stripped rank and title.

units.zh: 文盛旣失兵權，私懷怨望，世祖聞之，乃以下獄。
units.en: Stripped of command, he nursed grievance; Shizu heard and jailed him.
units.literal: Having lost military authority, he harbored private resentment; when Shizu heard, he was thrown into prison.

units.zh: 時任約被擒，與文盛同禁。
units.en: Ren Yue had been captured and shared his cell.
units.literal: At the time Ren Yue had been captured and was imprisoned with Wensheng.

units.zh: 文盛謂約曰：「汝何不早降，令我至此。」
units.en: Wensheng said to Yue, "Why did you not surrender sooner and spare me this?"
units.literal: Wensheng said to Yue: "Why did you not surrender early and put me in this plight?"

units.zh: 約曰：「門外不見卿馬跡，使我何遽得降？」
units.en: Yue said, "I saw no hoofprints of yours outside the gate—how could I surrender so soon?"
units.literal: Yue said: "Outside the gate one saw no trace of your horses—how was I to surrender at once?"

units.zh: 文盛無以答，遂死獄中。
units.en: Wensheng had no reply and died in prison.
units.literal: Wensheng had nothing to answer and died in prison.

units.zh: 杜崱，京兆杜陵人也。
units.en: Du Ze was from Dulings in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Du Ze, of Dulings in Jingzhao commandery.

units.zh: 其先自北歸南，居於雍州之襄陽，子孫因家焉。
units.en: His forebears came south from the north and settled at Xiangyang in Yong; the family remained there.
units.literal: His ancestors had returned south from the north and settled at Xiangyang in Yong province; descendants made their home there.

units.zh: 祖靈啓，齊給事中。
units.en: Grandfather Lingqi was a Qi court attendant.
units.literal: Grandfather Lingqi served Qi as attendant within the court.

units.zh: 父懷寶，少有志節，常邀際會。
units.en: His father Huaibao had spirit and principle from youth and waited for his hour.
units.literal: Father Huaibao from youth had resolve and integrity, always awaiting the right moment.

units.zh: 高祖義師東下，隨南平王偉留鎮襄陽。
units.en: When Gaozu's army marched east he stayed with Prince of Nanping Wei to hold Xiangyang.
units.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army marched east, he followed Prince of Nanping Wei remaining to garrison Xiangyang.

units.zh: 天監中，稍立功績，官至驍猛將軍、梁州刺史。
units.en: Under Heavenly Surveillance he rose through merit to General of Fierce Valor and Liang inspector.
units.literal: In Heavenly Surveillance he gradually achieved merit and reached General of Fierce Valor and inspector of Liang prefecture.

units.zh: 大同初，魏梁州刺史元羅舉州內附，懷寶復進督華州。
units.en: Early in Great Unity Yuan Luo, Wei inspector of Liang, surrendered; Huaibao was also made commander of Hua.
units.literal: At the beginning of Great Unity Wei inspector of Liang Yuan Luo surrendered the prefecture inward; Huaibao was further made superintending commander of Hua prefecture.

units.zh: 值秦州所部武興氐王楊紹反，懷寶擊破之。
units.en: Yang Shao, Di king of Wu Xing in Qin, rebelled; Huaibao defeated him.
units.literal: Qin prefecture's dependent Wu Xing had Di king Yang Shao rebel; Huaibao defeated and broke him.

units.zh: 五年，卒於鎮。
units.en: In the fifth year he died in office.
units.literal: In the fifth year he died at his post.

units.zh: 崱卽懷寶第七子也。
units.en: Ze was Huaibao's seventh son.
units.literal: Ze was Huaibao's seventh son.

units.zh: 幼有志氣，居鄉里以膽勇稱。
units.en: From youth he had nerve and was known at home for boldness.
units.literal: From youth he had fighting spirit and was known in his hometown for courage and daring.

units.zh: 釋褐廬江驃騎府中兵參軍。
units.en: He began as army recorder on the Lujiang Rapid Cavalry staff.
units.literal: On leaving the office he became army recorder in the Rapid Cavalry command of Lujiang.

units.zh: 世祖臨荊州，仍參幕府，後爲新興太守。
units.en: When Shizu held Jingzhou he served on his staff, later becoming governor of Xinxing.
units.literal: When Shizu governed Jingzhou he still served on his staff, later becoming governor of Xinxing.

units.zh: 太清二年，隨岳陽王來襲荊州，世祖以與之有舊，密邀之。
units.en: In Supreme Clarity year two he came with the Prince of Yueyang to attack Jingzhou; Shizu, who knew him of old, secretly called him over.
units.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity he followed the Prince of Yueyang in coming to raid Jingzhou; Shizu, having old ties with him, secretly invited him.

units.zh: 崱乃與兄岸、弟幼安、兄子龕等夜歸于世祖，世祖以爲持節、信威將軍、武州刺史。
units.en: Ze came by night with his brother An, younger brother You'an, and nephew Kan; Shizu made him staff bearer, General of Trustworthy Might, and Wu inspector.
units.literal: Ze then with his elder brother An, younger brother You'an, and nephew Kan by night returned to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, General of Trustworthy Might, and inspector of Wu prefecture.

units.zh: 俄遷宣毅將軍，領鎮蠻護軍、武陵內史，枝江縣侯，邑千戶。
units.en: Soon he became General Who Chastises the Yi, Barbarian-quelling Protector, interior minister of Wuling, and Marquis of Zhijiang with a thousand households.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred General Who Chastises the Yi, concurrently Barbarian-quelling Protector, interior minister of Wuling, and Marquis of Zhijiang with a fief of a thousand households.

units.zh: 令隨王僧辯東討侯景。
units.en: He was ordered to follow Wang Sengbian east against Hou Jing.
units.literal: He was ordered to follow Wang Sengbian east to campaign against Hou Jing.

units.zh: 至巴陵，會景來攻，數十日不剋而遁。
units.en: At Baling Hou Jing attacked; after many days he could not win and fled.
units.literal: Reaching Baling, Jing came to attack; for many days he could not take it and fled.

units.zh: 加侍中、左衛將軍，進爵爲公，增邑五百戶。
units.en: He was made palace attendant and Left Guard general, raised to duke, fief increased five hundred households.
units.literal: He was added palace attendant and Left Guard general, promoted in rank to duke, fief increased five hundred households.

units.zh: 仍隨僧辯追景至石頭，與賊相持橫嶺。
units.en: He followed Sengbian in pursuit to Stonehead and faced the bandit at Heng Ridge.
units.literal: He still followed Sengbian pursuing Jing to Stonehead, stalemate with the bandit at Heng Ridge.

units.zh: 及戰，景親率精銳，左右衝突，崱從嶺後橫截之，景乃大敗，東奔晉陵，崱入據城。
units.en: In the fight Jing led his best men in person; Ze struck from behind the ridge; Jing was shattered and fled east to Jinling; Ze took the city.
units.literal: In battle Jing personally led elites, charging left and right; Ze cut in from behind the ridge and Jing was greatly defeated, fleeing east to Jinling; Ze entered and held the city.

units.zh: 景平，加散騎常侍、持節、督江州諸軍事、江州刺史，增邑千戶。
units.en: When Jing fell he was added palace attendant, staff bearer, Jiang commander, and Jiang inspector—fief increased a thousand households.
units.literal: When Jing was pacified he was added regular palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander of Jiang military affairs, inspector of Jiang—fief increased a thousand households.

units.zh: 是月，齊將郭元建攻秦州刺史嚴超遠於秦郡，王僧辯令崱赴援。
units.en: That month Qi general Guo Yuanjian besieged Yan Chaoyuan at Qin; Wang Sengbian sent Ze to relieve him.
units.literal: That month Qi general Guo Yuanjian attacked Qin prefecture inspector Yan Chaoyuan at Qin commandery; Wang Sengbian ordered Ze to relieve him.

units.zh: 陳霸先亦自歐陽來會，與元建大戰于士林，霸先令強弩射，元建衆卻。
units.en: Chen Baxian came from Ouyang to join; at Shilin they fought Guo Yuanjian; Baxian ordered heavy crossbows and Yuanjian's men fell back.
units.literal: Chen Baxian also came from Ouyang to join; with Yuanjian they fought a great battle at Shilin; Baxian ordered strong crossbowmen to shoot and Yuanjian's host withdrew.

units.zh: 崱因縱兵擊，大破之，斬首萬餘級，生擒千餘人，元建收餘衆而遁。
units.en: Ze charged and broke them—ten thousand heads, a thousand prisoners; Yuanjian gathered what was left and fled.
units.literal: Ze then released his troops to strike, routing them greatly—more than ten thousand heads cut, more than a thousand captured alive; Yuanjian gathered the remnant and fled.

units.zh: 時世祖執王琳於江陵，其長史陸納等遂于長沙反，世祖徵崱與王僧辯討之。
units.en: Shizu held Wang Lin at Jiangling; Lu Na rebelled at Changsha; Shizu called Ze and Wang Sengbian to suppress him.
units.literal: At the time Shizu held Wang Lin at Jiangling; his chief clerk Lu Na and others then rebelled at Changsha; Shizu summoned Ze and Wang Sengbian to suppress them.

units.zh: 承聖二年，及納等戰於車輪，大敗，陷其二壘，納等走保長沙，崱等圍之。
units.en: In Chengsheng year two they fought Lu Na at Wheel Ford, took two forts, and drove him to Changsha; Ze besieged the city.
units.literal: In Chengsheng year two they fought Na and others at Wheel Ford, were greatly victorious, took two of their forts; Na and others fled to hold Changsha; Ze and the others besieged them.

units.zh: 後納等降，崱又與王僧辯西討武陵王於硤口，至卽破平之。
units.en: When Na surrendered Ze went west with Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Wuling at Gorge Mouth and broke him at once.
units.literal: Later Na and others surrendered; Ze again with Wang Sengbian campaigned west against the Prince of Wuling at Gorge Mouth—reaching there they broke and pacified him at once.

units.zh: 於是旋鎮，遘疾卒。
units.en: He returned to his post, fell ill, and died.
units.literal: Thereupon he returned to his command but met illness and died.

units.zh: 詔曰：「崱，京兆舊姓，元凱苗裔。
units.en: The edict said, "Ze, of the ancient house of Jingzhao, line of Yuan Kai.
units.literal: An edict said: "Ze—of the old surname of Jingzhao, descendant of Yuan Kai.

units.zh: 家傳學業，世載忠貞。
units.en: His clan carried learning; generation after generation served in loyalty.
units.literal: His family transmitted learning; generation after generation bore loyal fidelity.

units.zh: 自驅傳江渚，政號廉能。
units.en: From service on the river isles his rule was called clean and capable.
units.literal: From driving the relay-chariot on the river isles, his rule was called incorrupt and able.

units.zh: 推轂淺原，實聞清靜。
units.en: On the shallow fords of command one heard only of his quiet rule.
units.literal: Pushing the chariot-wheel on the shallow ford, one truly heard of his quiet governance.

units.zh: 奄致殞喪，惻愴于懷。
units.en: Suddenly he is gone—grief pierces the heart.
units.literal: Suddenly he met ruin and death—grief pierces the breast.

units.zh: 可贈車騎將軍，加鼓吹一部。
units.en: Let him be posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with martial music.
units.literal: He may be posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry, with one suite of martial music added.

units.zh: 諡曰武。」
units.en: Posthumous title: Martial."
units.literal: His posthumous title shall be Martial."

units.zh: 崱兄弟九人，兄嵩、岑、嵸、岌、嶷、巘、岸及弟幼安，並知名當世。
units.en: Ze had nine brothers—Song, Cen, Cong, Ji, Yi, Yan, An, and the younger You'an—all famed in their time.
units.literal: Ze had nine brothers—elder brothers Song, Cen, Cong, Ji, Yi, Yan and An, and younger brother You'an—all famous in their day.

units.zh: 岸，字公衡。
units.en: An, styled Gongheng.
units.literal: An, styled Gongheng.

units.zh: 少有武幹，好從橫之術。
units.en: From youth he had martial talent and loved bold stratagems.
units.literal: From youth he had martial capacity and loved schemes of alliance and pressure.

units.zh: 太清中，與崱同歸世祖，世祖以爲持節、平北將軍、北梁州刺史，封江陵縣侯，邑一千戶。
units.en: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze; Shizu made him staff bearer, Pacifying North general, North Liang inspector, and Marquis of Jiangling with a thousand households.
units.literal: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, Pacifying North general, inspector of North Liang, Marquis of Jiangling, fief a thousand households.

units.zh: 岸因請襲襄陽，世祖許之。
units.en: An asked to strike Xiangyang; Shizu agreed.
units.literal: An thereupon requested to raid Xiangyang; Shizu granted it.

units.zh: 岸乃晝夜兼行，先往攻其城，不剋。
units.en: He marched day and night and struck the city first—but could not take it.
units.literal: He marched day and night, first going to attack the city—but could not take it.

units.zh: 岳陽至，遂走依其兄巘于南陽，巘時爲南陽太守。
units.en: When the Prince of Yueyang came he fled to his brother Yan at Nanyang, who was then Nanyang governor.
units.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang arrived he fled to rely on his brother Yan at Nanyang—Yan was then governor of Nanyang.

units.zh: 岳陽尋遣攻陷其城，岸及巘俱遇害。
units.en: The prince soon took the city; An and Yan both perished.
units.literal: The Prince of Yueyang soon sent troops to take the city; An and Yan both met disaster.

units.zh: 幼安性至孝，寬厚，雄勇過人。
units.en: You'an was deeply filial, open-handed and mild, yet fiercer than most in battle.
units.literal: You'an was utterly filial by nature, generous and mild, and surpassed others in fierce courage.

units.zh: 太清中，與兄崱同歸世祖，世祖以爲雲麾將軍、西荊州刺史，封華容縣侯，邑一千戶。
units.en: In Supreme Clarity he returned with Ze; Shizu made him Cloud Banner general, West Jing inspector, and Marquis of Huarong with a thousand households.
units.literal: In Supreme Clarity he returned with his brother Ze to Shizu; Shizu made him Cloud Banner general, inspector of West Jing, Marquis of Huarong, fief a thousand households.

units.zh: 令與平南將軍王僧辯討河東王譽於長沙，平之。
units.en: He was ordered with Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong at Changsha and pacify him.
units.literal: He was ordered with Pacifying South general Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong Yu at Changsha and pacify him.

units.zh: 又命率精甲一萬，助左衛將軍徐文盛東討侯景。
units.en: He was also told to lead ten thousand armored men to aid Xu Wensheng against Hou Jing.
units.literal: He was also ordered to lead ten thousand picked armored troops to aid Left Guard general Xu Wensheng in the eastern campaign against Hou Jing.

units.zh: 至貝磯，遇景將任約來逆，遂與戰，大敗之。
units.en: At Shell Ford he met Ren Yue; they fought and broke him.
units.literal: Reaching Shell Ford he met Jing's general Ren Yue coming to resist; they fought and routed him greatly.

units.zh: 斬其儀同叱羅子通、湘州刺史趙威方等，傳首江陵。
units.en: They cut off Chiluo Zitong, Zhao Weifang of Xiangzhou, and others, and sent the heads to Jiangling.
units.literal: They beheaded his Staff Equal Chiluo Zitong, Xiangzhou inspector Zhao Weifang and others, and sent the heads to Jiangling.

units.zh: 乃進軍大舉，因與景相持。
units.en: Then the host pushed forward and faced Jing in stalemate.
units.literal: Thereupon the army advanced in force and stalemate with Jing.

units.zh: 別攻武昌，拔之。
units.en: He also attacked Wuchang and took it.
units.literal: Separately he attacked Wuchang and took it.

units.zh: 景渡蘆洲上流以壓文盛等，幼安與衆軍攻之，景大敗，盡獲其舟艦。
units.en: Jing moved above Reed Islet to crush Wensheng; You'an attacked with the army, shattered Jing, and seized every ship.
units.literal: Jing crossed upstream of Reed Islet to press Wensheng and the others; You'an with the host attacked and Jing was greatly defeated, all his boats captured.

units.zh: 會景密遣襲陷郢州，執刺史方諸等以歸，人情大駭，徐文盛由漢口遁歸，衆軍大敗，幼安遂降于景。
units.en: Then Jing sent raiders by a hidden road, took E prefecture, and captured Fang Zhu; panic spread; Wensheng fled up the Han; the army collapsed; You'an surrendered to Jing.
units.literal: Just then Jing secretly sent a raid that seized E prefecture, capturing inspector Fang Zhu and others and returning; morale was greatly shaken; Xu Wensheng fled by Hankou; the armies were utterly routed; You'an then surrendered to Jing.

units.zh: 景殺之，以其多反覆故也。
units.en: Jing killed him for his repeated betrayals.
units.literal: Jing killed him—for his many vacillations.

units.zh: 龕，崱第二兄岑之子。
units.en: Kan was son of Ze's second brother Cen.
units.literal: Kan was son of Ze's second elder brother Cen.

units.zh: 少驍勇，善用兵，亦太清中與諸父同歸世祖，世祖以爲持節、忠武將軍、鄖州刺史，中廬縣侯，邑一千戶。
units.en: From youth he was fierce and knew war; in Supreme Clarity he returned with his uncles; Shizu made him staff bearer, General of Loyal Martial, Yun inspector, and Marquis of Zhonglu with a thousand households.
units.literal: From youth fierce and brave, skilled at using troops; also in Supreme Clarity he returned with his uncles to Shizu; Shizu made him bearer of the staff, General of Loyal Martial, inspector of Yun, Marquis of Zhonglu, fief a thousand households.

units.zh: 與叔幼安俱隨王僧辯討河東王，平之。
units.en: With his uncle You'an he followed Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Hedong and pacified him.
units.literal: With his uncle You'an he followed Wang Sengbian to campaign against the Prince of Hedong and pacified him.

units.zh: 又隨僧辯下，繼徐文盛軍至巴陵，聞侯景襲陷郢州，西上將至，乃與僧辯等守巴陵以待之。
units.en: Following Sengbian downriver he took over Wensheng's line at Baling; hearing Jing had taken E and was coming west, he and Sengbian held Baling to meet him.
units.literal: Again following Sengbian downstream he continued Xu Wensheng's army to Baling; hearing Hou Jing had raided and seized E prefecture and was coming west, he with Sengbian and the others held Baling to await him.

units.zh: 景至，圍之數旬，不剋而遁。
units.en: Jing besieged it for weeks, failed, and fled.
units.literal: When Jing arrived he besieged it many weeks, could not take it, and fled.

units.zh: 遷太府卿、安北將軍、督定州諸軍事、定州刺史，加通直散騎常侍，增邑五百戶。
units.en: He became Grand Treasurer, Pacifying North general, Ding commander and inspector, Direct and Regular Palace Attendant, fief up five hundred households.
units.literal: He was transferred Grand Treasurer, Pacifying North general, commander of Ding military affairs, inspector of Ding, added Direct and Regular Palace Attendant, fief increased five hundred households.

units.zh: 仍隨僧辯追景至江夏，圍其城。
units.en: He followed Sengbian in pursuit to Jiangxia and besieged the city.
units.literal: He still followed Sengbian pursuing Jing to Jiangxia and besieged the city.

units.zh: 景將宋子仙棄城遁，龕追至楊浦，生擒之。
units.en: Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled; Kan chased to Yangpu and took him alive.
units.literal: Jing's general Song Zixian abandoned the city and fled; Kan pursued to Yangpu and captured him alive.

units.zh: 大寶三年，衆軍至姑孰，景將侯子鑒逆戰，龕與陳霸先、王琳等率精銳擊之，大敗子鑒，遂至於石頭。
units.en: In Great Treasure year three the armies reached Gushu; Hou Zijian met them; Kan with Chen Baxian and Wang Lin led elites, broke Zijian, and pushed on to Stonehead.
units.literal: In the third year of Great Treasure the armies reached Gushu; Jing's general Hou Zijian met them in battle; Kan with Chen Baxian, Wang Lin and others led crack troops to strike, routing Zijian greatly, and reached Stonehead.

units.zh: 景親率其黨會戰，龕與衆軍奮擊，大破景，景遂東奔。
units.en: Jing fought in person; Kan and the host struck hard, shattered him, and Jing fled east.
units.literal: Jing personally led his faction to join battle; Kan with the armies fought fiercely, routing Jing greatly; Jing fled east.

units.zh: 論功爲最，授平東將軍、東揚州刺史，益封一千戶。
units.en: His merit ranked first; he was made Pacifying East general, East Yang inspector, fief up a thousand households.
units.literal: For merit he was first; he was made Pacifying East general, inspector of East Yang, fief increased a thousand households.

units.zh: 承聖二年，又與王僧辯討陸納等於長沙，降之。
units.en: In Chengsheng year two he again followed Wang Sengbian against Lu Na at Changsha and forced surrender.
units.literal: In Chengsheng year two he again with Wang Sengbian suppressed Lu Na and others at Changsha and made them surrender.

units.zh: 又征武陵王於西陵，亦平之。
units.en: He also campaigned against the Prince of Wuling at Xiling and pacified him.
units.literal: Again he campaigned against the Prince of Wuling at Xiling and likewise pacified him.

units.zh: 後江陵陷，齊納貞陽侯以紹梁嗣，以龕爲震州刺史、吳興太守。
units.en: After Jiangling fell Qi set up the True Yang Marquis to continue Liang; Kan became Zhen inspector and Wuxing governor.
units.literal: Later Jiangling fell; Qi installed the True Yang Marquis to continue Liang; Kan was made inspector of Zhen and governor of Wuxing.

units.zh: 又除鎮南將軍、都督南豫州諸軍事、南豫州刺史、溧陽縣侯，給鼓吹一部。
units.en: He was also made Pacifying South general, South Yu commander and inspector, Marquis of Liyang, with martial music.
units.literal: Also made Pacifying South general, commander of South Yu military affairs, inspector of South Yu, Marquis of Liyang, given a suite of martial music.

units.zh: 又加散騎常侍、鎮東大將軍。
units.en: He was also made Regular Palace Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the East.
units.literal: Also added Regular Palace Attendant and Great General Who Pacifies the East.

units.zh: 會陳霸先襲陷京師，執王僧辯殺之。
units.en: Then Chen Baxian seized the capital, took Wang Sengbian, and killed him.
units.literal: Just then Chen Baxian raided and seized the capital, seized Wang Sengbian and killed him.

units.zh: 龕，僧辯之婿也，爲吳興太守。
units.en: Kan was Sengbian's son-in-law and governor of Wuxing.
units.literal: Kan, Sengbian's son-in-law, was governor of Wuxing.

units.zh: 以霸先旣非貴素，兵又猥雜，在軍府日，都不以霸先經心；
units.en: Baxian was low-born and his troops were a rabble; in headquarters days Kan never took him seriously;
units.literal: Because Baxian was not of noble birth and his troops were crude and mixed, in headquarters days Kan never took Baxian to heart;

units.zh: 及爲本郡，每以法繩其宗門，無所縱捨，霸先銜之切齒。
units.en: as home governor he bound his clan by law without mercy—Baxian hated him to the bone.
units.literal: when he became governor of his home commandery he constantly bound his clan by law without indulgence—Baxian hated him to the teeth.

units.zh: 及僧辯敗，龕乃據吳興以距之，遣軍副杜泰攻陳蒨於長城，反爲蒨所敗。
units.en: When Sengbian fell Kan held Wuxing against him and sent Du Tai to strike Chen Qian at Changcheng—but Qian beat him.
units.literal: When Sengbian was defeated Kan then held Wuxing to resist him, sending deputy Du Tai to attack Chen Qian at Changcheng—but was in turn defeated by Qian.

units.zh: 霸先乃遣將周文育討龕，龕令從弟北叟出距，又爲文育所破，走義興，霸先親率衆圍之。
units.en: Baxian sent Zhou Wenyun against him; Kan sent his cousin Beisou out and was beaten again; he fled to Yixing and Baxian besieged him in person.
units.literal: Baxian then sent general Zhou Wenyun to campaign against Kan; Kan sent his cousin Beisou out to resist and was again broken by Wenyun; he fled to Yixing and Baxian personally led troops to besiege him.

units.zh: 會齊將柳達摩等襲京師，霸先恐，遂還與齊人連和。
units.en: Then Liu Damo of Qi struck the capital; Baxian feared and turned back to treat with Qi.
units.literal: Just then Qi general Liu Damo and others raided the capital; Baxian was afraid and returned to ally with the Qi men.

units.zh: 龕聞齊兵還，乃降，遂遇害。
units.en: When Kan heard Qi had withdrawn he surrendered—and was killed.
units.literal: When Kan heard the Qi army had withdrawn he surrendered and then met disaster.

units.zh: 陰子春，字幼文，武威姑臧人也。
units.en: Yin Zichun, styled Youwen, was from Guzang in Wuwei.
units.literal: Yin Zichun, styled Youwen, was a man of Guzang in Wuwei commandery.

units.zh: 晉義熙末，曾祖襲，隨宋高祖南遷，至南平，因家焉。
units.en: At the end of Jin Yixi his great-grandfather Xi followed Song Gaozu south to Nanping and settled there.
units.literal: At the end of Yixi in Jin, his great-grandfather Xi followed Song Gaozu south, reaching Nanping, and there made home.

units.zh: 父智伯，與高祖鄰居，少相友善，嘗入高祖臥內，見有異光成五色，因握高祖手曰：「公後必大貴，非人臣也。
units.en: His father Zhibo lived next to Gaozu; they were friends from youth; once he entered Gaozu's bedchamber and saw a five-colored light; he took Gaozu's hand and said, "You are destined for greatness—not the fate of a subject.
units.literal: Father Zhibo was Gaozu's neighbor; from youth they were friendly; he once entered Gaozu's sleeping chamber and saw a strange light in five colors; he grasped Gaozu's hand and said: "Your Grace will surely rise to great nobility—not the lot of a subject.

units.zh: 天下方亂，安蒼生者，其在君乎！」
units.en: The realm is in chaos; will you not be the one to save the people?"
units.literal: The realm is in disorder; he who settles the black-haired folk—is it not you?"

units.zh: 高祖曰：「幸勿多言。」
units.en: Gaozu said, "Say no more."
units.literal: Gaozu said: "Pray speak no more."

units.zh: 於是情好轉密，高祖每有求索，如外府焉。
units.en: Their bond deepened; whenever Gaozu needed anything it was as if he had another treasury.
units.literal: Thereupon their affection grew still closer; whenever Gaozu had need it was as from an outer treasury.

units.zh: 及高祖踐阼，官至梁、秦二州刺史。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he rose to inspector of Liang and Qin.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he reached inspector of Liang and Qin.

units.zh: 子春，天監初，起家宣惠將軍、西陽太守。
units.en: Zichun began under Heavenly Surveillance as General of Manifest Grace and Xiyang governor.
units.literal: Zichun, at the beginning of Heavenly Surveillance, began office as General of Manifest Grace and governor of Xiyang.

units.zh: 普通中，累遷至明威將軍、南梁州刺史；
units.en: In the Ordinary era he rose to General of Bright Might and South Liang inspector;
units.literal: In the Ordinary era he was repeatedly promoted to General of Bright Might and inspector of South Liang;

units.zh: 又遷信威將軍、都督梁、秦、華三州諸軍事、梁、秦二州刺史。
units.en: then General of Trustworthy Might, commander of Liang, Qin, and Hua, and inspector of Liang and Qin.
units.literal: also transferred General of Trustworthy Might, commander of Liang, Qin, and Hua military affairs, inspector of Liang and Qin.

units.zh: 太清二年，討峽中叛蠻，平之。
units.en: In Supreme Clarity year two he put down rebel tribes in the gorges.
units.literal: In the second year of Supreme Clarity he campaigned against rebel barbarians in the gorges and pacified them.

units.zh: 徵爲左衛將軍，又遷侍中。
units.en: He was summoned as Left Guard general, then made palace attendant.
units.literal: He was summoned as Left Guard general, then transferred palace attendant.

units.zh: 屬侯景亂，世祖令子春隨領軍將軍王僧辯攻邵陵王於郢州，平之。
units.en: When Hou Jing rebelled Shizu ordered Zichun to follow Wang Sengbian against the Prince of Shaoling at E and pacify him.
units.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled Shizu ordered Zichun to follow General Who Commands the Army Wang Sengbian in attacking the Prince of Shaoling at E prefecture and pacifying him.

units.zh: 又與左衛將軍徐文盛東討侯景，至貝磯，與景遇，子春力戰，恒冠諸軍，頻敗景。
units.en: Again with Xu Wensheng he marched east against Hou Jing; at Shell Ford they met Jing; Zichun fought at the fore and beat him again and again.
units.literal: Again with Left Guard general Xu Wensheng he campaigned east against Hou Jing; reaching Shell Ford they met Jing; Zichun fought fiercely, always foremost among the armies, repeatedly defeating Jing.

units.zh: 值郢州陷沒，軍遂退敗。
units.en: When E prefecture fell the army retreated in rout.
units.literal: When E prefecture fell the armies then retreated in defeat.

units.zh: 大寶二年，卒於江陵。
units.en: In Great Treasure year two he died at Jiangling.
units.literal: In the second year of Great Treasure he died at Jiangling.

units.zh: 孫顥，少知名。
units.en: His grandson Hao was known while still young.
units.literal: His grandson Hao was known from youth.

units.zh: 釋褐奉朝請，歷尚書金部郎。
units.en: He began as Court Attendant on Duty and rose to director of the Jin Department in the Secretariat.
units.literal: On leaving office he was Court Attendant on Duty, successively Jin Department director in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 後入周。
units.en: Later he went over to Zhou.
units.literal: Later he entered Zhou.

units.zh: 撰《瓊林》二十卷。
units.en: He wrote Pavilions in Splendor in twenty scrolls.
units.literal: He compiled Pavilions in Splendor in twenty scrolls.

units.zh: 史臣曰：胡僧祐勇幹有聞，搴旗破敵者數矣；
units.en: The historian writes: Hu Sengyou was famed for courage; again and again he took the standard and broke the foe;
units.literal: The historian says: Hu Sengyou's bravery and capacity were renowned; several times he seized the standard and broke the enemy;

units.zh: 及捐軀殉節，殞身王事，雖古之忠烈，何以加焉。
units.en: when he gave his life for the throne—even the martyrs of old—who could surpass him?
units.literal: when he gave his body and died for his integrity in the king's service—even the loyal martyrs of antiquity—how could they surpass him?

units.zh: 徐文盛始立功績，不能終其成名，爲不義也。
units.en: Xu Wensheng won merit at first yet could not finish establishing his name—this was unrighteous.
units.literal: Xu Wensheng at first achieved merit yet could not finish establishing his name—injustice.

units.zh: 杜崱識機變之理，知向背之宜，加以身屢典軍，頻殄寇逆，勳庸顯著，卒爲中興功臣。
units.en: Du Ze read the moment and chose the right side; he led armies again and again and crushed rebels—bright merit, a pillar of restoration.
units.literal: Du Ze knew the principle of timely change and the fitness of turning toward or away; moreover he repeatedly commanded armies and often extinguished rebels and invaders—merit illustrious, dying a great minister of restoration.

units.zh: 義哉！
units.en: How righteous!
units.literal: Righteous indeed!

units.zh: 景敗，侍中趙思賢以璽投景南兗州刺史郭元建，送于術，故術以進焉。
units.en: When Jing was defeated, attendant-in-ordinary Zhao Sixian gave the seal to Jing's southern Yanzhou governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; thus Shu was able to present it.
units.literal: When Jing was defeated, Attendant Zhong Zhao Sixian cast the seal upon Jing's Southern Yanzhou Governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; therefore Shu presented it.

units.zh: 陳武帝遣將侯安都、周文育等誅琳，仍受梁禪。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Chen sent generals Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu to execute Lin, then accepted Liang's abdication.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Chen sent Generals Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu to execute Lin, then accepted Liang's abdication.

units.zh: 逆戰於沌口，琳乘平肩輿，執鉞而麾之，禽安都、文育，其餘無所漏。
units.en: They fought upstream at Zhunkou. Lin rode a level-shouldered litter, grasped an axe and directed them, capturing Andu and Wenyu; of the rest none escaped.
units.literal: They fought upstream at Zhunkou; Lin rode a level-shouldered litter, grasped an axe and directed them, capturing Andu and Wenyu; of the rest none escaped.

units.zh: 鎖安都、文育置琳所坐艦中，令一閹豎監守之。
units.en: He shackled Andu and Wenyu aboard the vessel where Lin sat and set a eunuch to guard them.
units.literal: He shackled Andu and Wenyu aboard the vessel where Lin sat and set a eunuch to guard them.

units.zh: 安都、文育等盡逃還建業。
units.en: Andu, Wenyu, and the rest all escaped back to Jiankang.
units.literal: Andu, Wenyu, and the rest all escaped back to Jiankang.

units.zh: 昕少與邢卲俱為元羅賓友，及守東萊，卲舉室就之。
units.en: In youth Xin and Xing Shao had both been guests of Yuan Luo; when Xin held Donglai, Shao brought his whole household to join him.
units.literal: In youth Xin and Xing Shao had both been guests of Yuan Luo; when Xin held Donglai, Shao brought his whole household to join him.

units.zh: 時僧辯女婿杜龕鎮吳興，高祖乃使世祖還長城，立柵備龕，又使恪還武康，招集兵眾。
units.en: Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan then held Wuxing. The Founder sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to build defenses against him and sent Ke back to Wukang to raise men.
units.literal: At the time Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan garrisoned Wuxing, so the Founder sent Emperor Wen back to Changcheng to set up palisades against Kan, and also sent Ke back to Wukang to gather troops.

units.zh: 遷平西邵陵王長史。
units.en: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.
units.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.

units.zh: 起家梁祕書郎，歷太子舍人，輕車河東王主簿，安前邵陵王、中軍宣
units.en: He began as a Liang secretariat gentleman, then served as crown prince aide, registrar to the prince of Hedong of the light chariots, and merit clerk in the households of the former prince of Shaoling and the central army prince Xuan
units.literal: He first entered office as a Liang Secretariat Gentleman, then served as Aide to the Crown Prince, Registrar to the Prince of Hedong of the Light Chariots, and Merit Clerk in the two prefectures of the preceding Prince of Shaoling and the Central Army Prince Xuan

units.zh: 安前邵陵王中軍宣
units.en: Preceding prince of Shaoling, central army prince Xuan
units.literal: Preceding Prince of Shaoling, Central Army Prince Xuan

units.zh: 六年正月，師次義陽，遇荊州陷，因略地南至郢州，獲梁州刺史司徒陸法和，仍剋郢州。
units.en: In the first month of the sixth year, the army halted at Yiyang. When Jing Province fell, they raided south as far as Ying Province, captured Lu Fahe, Inspector of Liang Province and Minister of State, and then took Ying Province.
units.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, the army halted at Yiyang. When Jing Province fell, they raided south as far as Ying Province, captured Lu Fahe, Inspector of Liang Province and Minister of State, and then took Ying Province.

units.zh: 岳先送法和於京師，遣儀同慕容儼據郢城。
units.en: Yue first sent Fahé to the capital and dispatched honorary equal Murong Yan to hold Ying city.
units.literal: Yue first sent Fahé to the capital and dispatched Honorary Equal Murong Yan to hold Ying city.

units.zh: 王僧辯之討侯景也，王琳為前軍，琳與瑒同門，乃表薦為戎昭將軍、宜都太守，仍從僧辯救徐文盛於武昌。
units.en: When Wang Sengbian attacked Hou Jing, Wang Lin led the van. Lin and Yang were schoolmates; Lin recommended him as martial-announcements general and administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to relieve Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.
units.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Wang Lin was vanguard; Lin and Yang were of the same gate, and Lin memorialized recommending him as Martial-Announcements General and Administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to rescue Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.

units.zh: 陳慶之 蘭欽
units.en: Chen Qingzhi; Lan Qin
units.literal: Chen Qingzhi; Lan Qin

units.zh: 陳慶之字子雲，義興國山人也。
units.en: Chen Qingzhi, styled Ziyun, came from Guoshan in Yixing commandery.
units.literal: Chen Qingzhi, styled Ziyun, was a native of Guoshan in Yixing.

units.zh: 諡曰武。
units.en: His posthumous title was Martial.
units.literal: His posthumous name was Martial.

units.zh: 普通中，魏徐州刺史元法僧于彭城求入內附，以慶之爲武威將軍，與胡龍牙、成景儁率諸軍應接。
units.en: During the Putong reign, Yuan Faseng, the Wei inspector of Xu province, asked at Pengcheng to defect to Liang. Qingzhi was named General of Martial Prestige and, with Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun, led troops to take him in.
units.literal: In the Putong era, Yuan Faseng, Inspector of Xu province under Wei, at Pengcheng sought to enter and submit to the court; Qingzhi was made General of Martial Prestige and, with Hu Longya and Cheng Jingjun, led the armies to meet and receive him.

units.zh: 普通七年，安西將軍元樹出征壽春，除慶之假節、總知軍事。
units.en: In the seventh year of Putong, General Yuan Shu of the west marched on Shouchun. Qingzhi received acting credentials and overall command of the campaign.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Putong, Anxi General Yuan Shu campaigned against Shouchun; Qingzhi was given acting credentials and overall command of military affairs.

units.zh: 大通元年，隸領軍曹仲宗伐渦陽。
units.en: In the first year of Datong he served under Commander-in-Chief Cao Zhongzong in the attack on Guoyang.
units.literal: In the first year of Datong, he was attached to the army of the Commander-in-Chief Cao Zhongzong in the campaign against Guoyang.

units.zh: 大通初，魏北海王元顥以本朝大亂，自拔來降，求立爲魏主。
units.en: Early in Datong, Prince Hao of Beihai under Wei, citing turmoil at home, defected to Liang and asked to be set up as emperor of Wei.
units.literal: At the beginning of Datong, Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai under Wei, because his own dynasty was in great disorder, came over of his own accord to surrender and asked to be established as ruler of Wei.

units.zh: 高祖納之，以慶之爲假節、飆勇將軍，送元顥還北。
units.en: Emperor Wu agreed and named Qingzhi acting-credentials holder and General of Swift Valor to escort Hao north.
units.literal: The High Ancestor accepted this and made Qingzhi acting-credentials holder and General of Swift Valor, to escort Yuan Hao back north.

units.zh: 中大通二年，除都督南北司西豫豫四州諸軍事、南北司二州刺史，餘並如故。
units.en: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was made commander of the four provinces of Southern and Northern Si, Western Yu, and Yu, and inspector of Southern and Northern Si; his other posts remained unchanged.
units.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was appointed Commander of military affairs for the four provinces of Southern and Northern Si, Western Yu, and Yu, and Inspector of the two provinces of Southern and Northern Si; the rest remained as before.

units.zh: 大同二年，魏遣將侯景率衆七萬寇楚州，刺史桓和陷沒，景仍進軍淮上，貽慶之書使降。
units.en: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent Hou Jing with seventy thousand men against Chu. Inspector Huan He was overrun. Jing pushed on to the Huai and wrote Qingzhi urging surrender.
units.literal: In the second year of Datong, Wei sent the general Hou Jing with seventy thousand men to raid Chu province; Inspector Huan He was lost, and Jing still advanced his army on the Huai and sent Qingzhi a letter urging him to surrender.

units.zh: 五年十月，卒，時年五十六。
units.en: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, aged fifty-six.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year he died, at the age of fifty-six.

units.zh: 長子昭嗣。
units.en: His eldest son was Zhaosi.
units.literal: His eldest son was Zhaosi.

units.zh: 第五子昕，字君章。
units.en: His fifth son was Xin, styled Junzhang.
units.literal: His fifth son was Xin, styled Junzhang.

units.zh: 從高祖東下平建鄴，稍爲主書，散財聚士，常思效用。
units.en: When Emperor Wu marched east to take Jianye, Qingzhi followed. He rose to chief secretary, spent his fortune gathering followers, and always looked for a chance to prove himself.
units.literal: Following the High Ancestor east to pacify Jianye, he gradually became Chief Secretary, dispersed his wealth to gather gentlemen, and constantly thought of rendering service.

units.zh: 幼而隨從高祖。
units.en: From childhood he attended Emperor Wu.
units.literal: In his youth he followed and attended the High Ancestor.

units.zh: 高祖性好棊，每從夜達旦不輟，等輩皆倦寐，惟慶之不寢，聞呼卽至，甚見親賞。
units.en: Emperor Wu loved weiqi and often played from dusk until dawn. His attendants all fell asleep from exhaustion, but Qingzhi alone stayed awake and answered every summons—behind this lay deep personal regard.
units.literal: The High Ancestor loved weiqi; he would play from night until dawn without stopping, and his companions all grew weary and slept, but only Qingzhi did not sleep; at a call he would arrive at once, and was greatly favored and prized.

units.zh: 除奉朝請。
units.en: He was made a palace attendant.
units.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 還，除宣猛將軍、文德主帥，仍率軍二千，送豫章王綜入鎮徐州。
units.en: After returning he was made General of Manifest Valor and commander of the Civil Virtue corps, and again led two thousand men to install Prince Zong of Yuzhang as garrison commander at Xu province.
units.literal: On his return he was appointed General of Manifest Valor and Commander of Civil Virtue, and still led two thousand troops to escort Prince Zong of Yuzhang to take up garrison at Xu province.

units.zh: 慶之進薄其壘，一鼓便潰。
units.en: Qingzhi pressed the stockade; a single charge broke it.
units.literal: Qingzhi advanced and pressed close to his stockade; at one drumbeat it collapsed.

units.zh: 慶之乃斬關夜退，軍士得全。
units.en: Qingzhi cut through the passes and withdrew by night, bringing the troops out intact.
units.literal: Qingzhi then cut through the passes and withdrew by night, and the soldiers were preserved whole.

units.zh: 慶之攻之，憲力屈遂降，慶之入據其城。
units.en: Qingzhi attacked them. When Xian's strength gave out he surrendered, and Qingzhi occupied his towns.
units.literal: Qingzhi attacked them; Xian's strength was exhausted and he then surrendered, and Qingzhi entered and seized his cities.

units.zh: 轉東宮直閤，賜爵關中侯。
units.en: He was made a direct attendant in the Eastern Palace and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanzhong.
units.literal: He was transferred to Direct Attendant of the Eastern Palace and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanzhong.

units.zh: 慶之曰：「魏人遠來，皆已疲倦，去我旣遠，必不見疑，及其未集，須挫其氣，出其不意，必無不敗之理。
units.en: Qingzhi said, "The Wei troops have marched far and are already tired. They think we are still distant and will not expect a strike. Before they mass, we must break their spirit and hit them unawares—defeat is certain.
units.literal: Qingzhi said: "The Wei men have come from afar and are all already weary; they are already far from us and surely will not suspect us—before they have gathered, we must blunt their spirit and take them unawares; there is surely no principle by which we would not defeat them.

units.zh: 且聞虜所據營，林木甚盛，必不夜出。
units.en: Besides, their camp stands in thick woods—they will not march out at night.
units.literal: Moreover I hear that the camp the barbarians hold has very dense woods and they surely will not come out at night.

units.zh: 諸君若疑惑，慶之請獨取之。」
units.en: If you still doubt me, let me take them alone."
units.literal: If you gentlemen are in doubt, Qingzhi asks to take it alone."

units.zh: 時滎陽未拔，士衆皆恐，慶之乃解鞍秣馬，宣喻衆曰：「吾至此以來，屠城略地，實爲不少；
units.en: Yingyang still held, and the men were afraid. Qingzhi had the horses unsaddled and fed, then addressed the army: "Since we crossed the border we have sacked cities and seized land without number;
units.literal: At that time Yingyang was not yet taken and officers and masses were all afraid; Qingzhi then unslung his saddle and fed his horses, and announced to the masses: "From the time I came here until now, cities slaughtered and territory seized have truly been not a few;

units.zh: 君等殺人父兄，略人子女，又爲無算。
units.en: you have killed fathers and elder brothers and taken sons and daughters beyond counting.
units.literal: you gentlemen have killed men's fathers and elder brothers and seized men's sons and daughters—again beyond counting.

units.zh: 天穆之衆，並是仇讎。
units.en: Tianmu's host are nothing but blood enemies.
units.literal: Tianmu's masses are all blood enemies.

units.zh: 我等才有七千，虜衆三十餘萬，今日之事，義不圖存。
units.en: We are seven thousand against more than three hundred thousand. Today we fight with no thought of survival.
units.literal: We have only seven thousand; the barbarian masses are more than three hundred thousand—today's affair, by right we do not plan to survive.

units.zh: 吾以虜騎不可爭力平原，及未盡至前，須平其城壘，諸君無假狐疑，自貽屠膾。」
units.en: Their cavalry cannot match us on open ground, but not until they are all here. Take the city first. Do not hesitate and make yourselves meat for the pot."
units.literal: I hold that barbarian horse cannot contend for strength on the plain; before they have all arrived, we must level their city and stockades—you gentlemen must not borrow fox-like doubt and bring down slaughter and mince upon yourselves."

units.zh: 於是與麾下二百騎奔擊，破其前軍，魏人震恐。
units.en: He then led two hundred horsemen in a headlong charge, routed the vanguard, and threw the Wei army into panic.
units.literal: Thereupon with two hundred horsemen under his command he charged in assault, broke their vanguard, and the Wei men were shaken with terror.

units.zh: 慶之乃還與諸將連營而進，據渦陽城，與魏軍相持。
units.en: Qingzhi rejoined the other commanders, advanced in linked camps, took Guoyang, and settled into a standoff with the Wei forces.
units.literal: Qingzhi then returned and, with the other generals linking camps, advanced and seized Guoyang city, and faced the Wei army in stalemate.

units.zh: 慶之杖節軍門曰：「共來至此，涉歷一歲，糜費糧仗，其數極多。
units.en: Qingzhi stood at the camp gate with his staff of authority and said, "We have all been here a full year. The grain and arms we have spent are beyond counting.
units.literal: Qingzhi, staff of authority in hand at the army gate, said: "Together we have come to this place and passed a full year; grain and weapons wasted—the number is extremely great.

units.zh: 諸軍並無鬭心，皆謀退縮，豈是欲立功名，直聚爲抄暴耳。
units.en: The troops have no will to fight and only want to retreat. You did not come here for glory—you came to loot.
units.literal: The armies all have no fighting spirit and all plan to shrink back—how could this be wishing to establish merit and fame? You have simply gathered to plunder and ravage.

units.zh: 吾聞置兵死地，乃可求生，須虜大合，然後與戰。
units.en: They say armies on deadly ground fight to live. Wait until the enemy masses, then fight.
units.literal: I have heard that placing troops on deadly ground is how one may seek life; we must wait until the barbarians have gathered in full, and then give battle.

units.zh: 審欲班師，慶之別有密敕，今日犯者，便依明詔。」
units.en: If you mean to withdraw, I hold a secret order from the throne: anyone who retreats today dies by imperial command."
units.literal: If you truly wish to withdraw the army, Qingzhi has a separate secret edict: whoever offends today shall be dealt with according to the clear decree."

units.zh: 魏人掎角作十三城，慶之銜枚夜出，陷其四壘，渦陽城主王緯乞降。
units.en: The Wei built thirteen linked strongpoints. Qingzhi led a silent night sortie, took four of them, and Guoyang's commander Wang Wei surrendered.
units.literal: The Wei men set up thirteen cities in pincer formation; Qingzhi went out at night with gags in the men's mouths, took four of their stockades, and Wang Wei, lord of Guoyang, begged to surrender.

units.zh: 所餘九城，兵甲猶盛，乃陳其俘馘，鼓噪而攻之，遂大奔潰，斬獲略盡，渦水咽流，降城中男女三萬餘口。
units.en: The other nine posts still held strong garrisons. He paraded prisoners and severed heads, stormed them with drum and shout, and drove them into rout. The slaughter filled the Guo River; more than thirty thousand men and women in the surrendered towns came over.
units.literal: Of the remaining nine cities the armor and weapons were still strong; he then displayed their captives and severed ears, attacked with drums and shouts, and they thereupon fled in great rout; those slain and captured were nearly all, the Guo River choked with the flow, and men and women of the surrendered cities numbered more than thirty thousand.

units.zh: 高祖嘉焉，賜慶之手詔曰：「本非將種，又非豪家，觖望風雲，以至於此。
units.en: Emperor Wu was delighted and sent Qingzhi a personal note: "You were born neither to a general's house nor to a great clan, yet you reached for wind and cloud and have come this far.
units.literal: The High Ancestor praised this and bestowed on Qingzhi a handwritten edict saying: "By origin you were not of a general's line, nor of a great house; you aspired to wind and cloud and have come to this.

units.zh: 可深思奇略，善克令終。
units.en: Think hard on bold strategy and see your career through to a worthy end.
units.literal: You may deeply ponder strange stratagems and well achieve a fine end.

units.zh: 開朱門而待賓，揚聲名於竹帛，豈非大丈夫哉！」
units.en: Open your gates to guests and let your name live in the histories—is that not the mark of a true man?"
units.literal: Open vermilion gates and await guests; raise your name on bamboo and silk—is this not a great man!"

units.zh: 顥于渙水卽魏帝號，授慶之使持節、鎮北將軍、護軍、前軍大都督，發自銍縣，進拔滎城，遂至睢陽。
units.en: At the Huan River, Hao took the Wei imperial title and gave Qingzhi full credentials as General Who Pacifies the North, army protector, and grand commander of the vanguard. They marched from Zhi county, took Yingcheng, and reached Suiyang.
units.literal: Hao at the Huan River assumed the title of Emperor of Wei and invested Qingzhi as bearer of credentials, General Who Pacifies the North, Protector of the Army, and Grand Commander of the Forward Army; setting out from Zhi county, he advanced and took Yingcheng, and then reached Suiyang.

units.zh: 慶之攻之，自旦至申，陷其三壘，大千乃降。
units.en: Qingzhi attacked from dawn until mid-afternoon, took three strongpoints, and Daqian surrendered.
units.literal: Qingzhi attacked him; from dawn to the shen hour he took three stockades, and Daqian then surrendered.

units.zh: 慶之命浮水築壘，攻陷其城，生擒暉業，獲租車七千八百兩。
units.en: Qingzhi built floating stockades across the water, stormed the city, took Yuye alive, and seized seventy-eight hundred tax wagons.
units.literal: Qingzhi ordered floating works to build stockades on the water, attacked and took his city, captured Yuye alive, and obtained seven thousand eight hundred tax carts.

units.zh: 顥進慶之衛將軍、徐州刺史、武都公。
units.en: Hao promoted him to General of the Guard, inspector of Xu province, and Duke of Wudu.
units.literal: Hao promoted Qingzhi to General of the Guard, Inspector of Xu province, and Duke of Wudu.

units.zh: 一鼓悉使登城，壯士東陽宋景休、義興魚天湣逾堞而入，遂克之。
units.en: At a single drumbeat he sent them up the walls. Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing scrambled over the parapet and broke in; the city fell.
units.literal: At one drumbeat he had them all mount the wall; the stalwart Song Jingxiu of Dongyang and Yu Tianmin of Yixing crossed the parapet and entered, and thereupon took it.

units.zh: 俄而魏陣外合，慶之率騎三千背城逆戰，大破之，魯安於陣乞降，元天穆、尒朱吐沒兒單騎獲免。
units.en: Soon the Wei encirclement closed. Qingzhi led three thousand horse out from the city and shattered them. Lu An surrendered in the field; Tianmu and Tumener fled alone on horseback.
units.literal: Shortly the Wei battle lines closed from outside; Qingzhi led three thousand horse with the city at his back to meet them in battle and routed them greatly; Lu An begged to surrender on the field, and Yuan Tianmu and Erzhu Tumener escaped on single horses.

units.zh: 進赴虎牢，尒朱世隆棄城走。
units.en: They advanced on Hulao; Erzhu Shilong abandoned the town and fled.
units.literal: Advancing to Hulao, Erzhu Shilong abandoned the city and fled.

units.zh: 顥以慶之爲侍中、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫，增邑萬戶。
units.en: Hao made Qingzhi palace attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and left grand master of splendid happiness, adding ten thousand households to his fief.
units.literal: Hao made Qingzhi Palace Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and increased his fief by ten thousand households.

units.zh: 魏大將軍上黨王元天穆、王老生、李叔仁又率衆四萬，攻陷大梁，分遣老生、費穆兵二萬，據虎牢，刁宣、刁雙入梁、宋，慶之隨方掩襲，並皆降款。
units.en: Grand General Prince Tianmu of Shangdang, Wang Laosheng, and Li Shuren marched again with forty thousand, took Daliang, and sent Laosheng and Fei Mu with twenty thousand to hold Hulao while Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang pushed into Liang and Song. Qingzhi ambushed them wherever they moved, and they all surrendered.
units.literal: The Wei Grand General Prince Tianmu of Shangdang, Yuan Tianmu, Wang Laosheng, and Li Shuren again led forty thousand men, attacked and took Daliang, and separately sent Laosheng and Fei Mu with twenty thousand troops to hold Hulao; Diao Xuan and Diao Shuang entered Liang and Song—Qingzhi struck by surprise wherever they went, and all submitted.

units.zh: 高祖復賜手詔稱美焉。
units.en: Emperor Wu sent another personal note of praise.
units.literal: The High Ancestor again bestowed a handwritten edict praising him.

units.zh: 慶之麾下悉著白袍，所向披靡。
units.en: Qingzhi's men all wore white robes and swept aside everything before them.
units.literal: All under Qingzhi's command wore white robes; wherever they went, none could stand before them.

units.zh: 先是洛陽童謠曰：「名師大將莫自牢，千兵萬馬避白袍。」
units.en: A Luoyang children's rhyme had already run: "Famed commanders, do not think yourselves safe—thousands upon thousands flee the white robes."
units.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme in Luoyang said: "Famed generals and great commanders, do not hold yourselves secure—thousands of soldiers and ten thousands of horses avoid the white robes."

units.zh: 自發銍縣至於洛陽，十四旬平三十二城，四十七戰，所向無前。
units.en: From Zhi county to Luoyang, in a hundred and forty days he took thirty-two cities in forty-seven battles and met no equal.
units.literal: From setting out at Zhi county until Luoyang, in fourteen tens of days he pacified thirty-two cities and forty-seven battles—wherever he went, none stood before him.

units.zh: 乃說顥曰：「今遠來至此，未伏尚多，若人知虛實，方更連兵，而安不忘危，須預爲其策。
units.en: He urged Hao, "We are far from home and many regions are not yet pacified. Once the enemy learns how few we are, they will mass again. In peace one must plan for danger.
units.literal: He then urged Hao: "Now having come from afar to this place, those not yet subdued are still many; if men know our emptiness and fullness, they will again link armies—in security do not forget peril; we must prepare plans in advance.

units.zh: 宜啓天子，更請精兵；
units.en: Ask the Son of Heaven for more elite troops;
units.literal: We ought to report to the Son of Heaven and request elite troops again;

units.zh: 並勒諸州，有南人沒此者，悉須部送。」
units.en: and order every province to send south all southerners held captive in the north."
units.literal: and also order the provinces that any southerners taken captive here must all be escorted and sent."

units.zh: 慶之不從。
units.en: Qingzhi refused.
units.literal: Qingzhi did not follow.

units.zh: 顥前以慶之爲徐州刺史，因固求之鎮。
units.en: Hao had already named Qingzhi inspector of Xu, and Qingzhi pressed hard to take up that post.
units.literal: Hao had earlier made Qingzhi Inspector of Xu province, and Qingzhi therefore firmly requested to garrison there.

units.zh: 顥心憚之，遂不遣。
units.en: Hao feared to let him go and refused.
units.literal: Hao feared him in his heart and therefore did not send him.

units.zh: 慶之渡河守北中郎城，三日中十有一戰，傷殺甚衆。
units.en: Qingzhi crossed the river and held Beizhonglang fortress. In three days he fought eleven engagements with heavy casualties on both sides.
units.literal: Qingzhi crossed the river and guarded Beizhonglang city; in three days there were eleven battles, and the wounded and slain were very many.

units.zh: 慶之馬步數千，結陣東反，榮親自來追，值蒿高山水洪溢，軍人死散。
units.en: Qingzhi withdrew east with a few thousand horse and foot. Erzhu Rong pursued in person. Floods on the Song and Gaoshan ranges drowned and scattered his army.
units.literal: Qingzhi had several thousand horse and foot; he formed battle lines and turned east in retreat. Rong came in person to pursue; they met with floods overflowing the Song Mountains and Gaoshan waters, and soldiers died and scattered.

units.zh: 慶之乃落鬚髮爲沙門，間行至豫州，豫州人程道雍等潛送出汝陰。
units.en: He shaved his beard, took monk's robes, and stole his way to Yu province, where Cheng Daoyong and others smuggled him out through Ruyin.
units.literal: Qingzhi then cut off his beard and hair and became a monk, traveling by secret paths to Yu province; Cheng Daoyong and others of Yu province secretly escorted him out through Ruyin.

units.zh: 至都，仍以功除右衛將軍，封永興縣侯，邑一千五百戶。
units.en: Back in the capital he was made General of the Right Guard for his service and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
units.literal: On reaching the capital, he was again appointed by merit as General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxing with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 出爲持節、都督緣淮諸軍事、奮武將軍、北兗州刺史。
units.en: He was sent out with credentials as commander of Huai frontier forces, General of Stirring Martiality, and inspector of Northern Yan.
units.literal: He went out as bearer of credentials, Commander of all military affairs along the Huai, General of Stirring Martiality, and Inspector of Northern Yan province.

units.zh: 慶之受命而行。
units.en: Qingzhi took his orders and marched.
units.literal: Qingzhi received the command and set out.

units.zh: 曾未浹辰，斬伯龍、僧強，傳其首。
units.en: Within ten days he had beheaded Bolong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads to court.
units.literal: Before a full ten days had passed, he beheaded Bolong and Seng Qiang and sent their heads.

units.zh: 慶之至鎮，遂圍懸瓠。
units.en: On reaching his post Qingzhi at once besieged Xuanhu.
units.literal: When Qingzhi reached his commandery, he thereupon besieged Xuanhu.

units.zh: 破魏潁州刺史婁起、揚州刺史是云寶於溱水，又破行臺孫騰、大都督侯進、豫州刺史堯雄、梁州刺史司馬恭於楚城。
units.en: He routed Wei Inspector of Ying Province Lou Qi and Inspector of Yang Province Shiyun Bao on the Qin River, then defeated mobile headquarters commander Sun Teng, Grand Commander Hou Jin, Inspector of Yu Province Yao Xiong, and Inspector of Liang Province Sima Gong at Chucheng.
units.literal: He defeated Wei Inspector of Ying province Lou Qi and Inspector of Yang province Shiyun Bao at the Qin River, and again defeated Mobile Headquarters Sun Teng, Grand Commander Hou Jin, Inspector of Yu province Yao Xiong, and Inspector of Liang province Sima Gong at Chucheng.

units.zh: 罷義陽鎮兵，停水陸轉運，江湖諸州並得休息。
units.en: He stood down the Yiyang garrison, halted supply convoys by land and water, and gave the river provinces a respite.
units.literal: He dismissed the garrison troops of Yiyang, halted water and land transport of supplies, and the provinces of the rivers and lakes all obtained rest.

units.zh: 開田六千頃，二年之後，倉廩充實。
units.en: He opened six thousand qing of farmland; within two years the granaries were full.
units.literal: He opened six thousand qing of fields; after two years the granaries were full and solid.

units.zh: 高祖每嘉勞之。
units.en: Emperor Wu repeatedly praised and rewarded him.
units.literal: The High Ancestor often praised and comforted him.

units.zh: 又表省南司州，復安陸郡，置上明郡。
units.en: He also memorialized to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and create Shangming commandery.
units.literal: He also memorialized to abolish Southern Si province, restore Anlu commandery, and establish Shangming commandery.

units.zh: 敕遣湘潭侯退、右衛夏侯夔等赴援，軍至黎漿，慶之已擊破景。
units.en: The court sent Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, Xiahou Kui of the Right Guard, and others to reinforce him, but by the time they reached Lijiang Qingzhi had already beaten Jing.
units.literal: An edict sent Marquis Tui of Xiangtan, Xiahou Kui of the Right Guard, and others to relieve them; when the army reached Lijiang, Qingzhi had already routed Jing.

units.zh: 時大寒雪，景棄輜重走，慶之收之以歸。
units.en: In bitter cold and snow Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled. Qingzhi gathered the spoils and returned.
units.literal: At that time there was great cold and snow; Jing abandoned his baggage train and fled, and Qingzhi gathered it and returned.

units.zh: 進號仁威將軍。
units.en: He was promoted to General of Humane Prestige.
units.literal: His title was advanced to General of Humane Prestige.

units.zh: 是歲，豫州饑，慶之開倉賑給，多所全濟。
units.en: That year Yu province suffered famine. Qingzhi opened the granaries and saved many lives.
units.literal: That year Yu province suffered famine; Qingzhi opened the granaries for relief and distribution, and many were wholly saved.

units.zh: 州民李升等八百人表請樹碑頌德，詔許焉。
units.en: Eight hundred residents led by Li Sheng petitioned for a stele in his honor, and the court approved.
units.literal: Eight hundred common people of the province, Li Sheng and others, submitted a memorial requesting a stele to praise his virtue, and an edict permitted it.

units.zh: 贈散騎常侍、左衛將軍，鼓吹一部。
units.en: He was posthumously made attendant cavalier at large and general of the left guard, with a full military band for his funeral.
units.literal: Posthumously he was given Attendant Cavalier at Large and General of the Left Guard, and one set of martial music.

units.zh: 慶之性祗慎，衣不紈綺，不好絲竹，射不穿札，馬非所便，而善撫軍士，能得其死力。
units.en: Qingzhi was sober and modest: no fine silks, no music, no skill at archery or horsemanship—yet he knew how to win soldiers' hearts and draw their utmost loyalty.
units.literal: Qingzhi's nature was respectful and cautious; he did not wear silk damask, did not love string and bamboo music, in archery could not pierce a leaf, and horse riding was not his forte—yet he was good at soothing soldiers and could obtain their strength unto death.

units.zh: 史臣曰：陳慶之、蘭欽俱有將略，戰勝攻取，蓋頗、牧、衛、霍之亞歟。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Chen Qingzhi and Lan Qin both possessed true generalship. In victory and conquest they stand in the company of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing.
units.literal: The historiographer says: Chen Qingzhi and Lan Qin both had military strategy; victorious in battle and taking by assault—they were perhaps the peers of Lian Po, Li Mu, Wei Qing, and Huo Qubing.

units.zh: 慶之警悟，早侍高祖，旣預舊恩，加之謹肅，蟬冕組珮，亦一世之榮矣。
units.en: Qingzhi was quick-witted and attended Emperor Wu from youth. Old favor, sober conduct, and the regalia of high office were glory enough for one life.
units.literal: Qingzhi was alert and perceptive; he early attended the High Ancestor, and having shared in old favor, together with his respectful sobriety, cicada cap and ribbon pendant—these too were the glory of a lifetime.

units.zh: 慶之欲逆戰，韋放以賊之前鋒必是輕銳，與戰若捷，不足爲功，如其不利，沮我軍勢，兵法所謂以逸待勞，不如勿擊。
units.en: Qingzhi wanted to give battle. Wei Fang objected that the enemy vanguard would be picked troops: a victory would count for little, a defeat would sap the army's spirit. Better, as the strategists say, to let the weary come to you—do not engage.
units.literal: Qingzhi wished to meet them in battle; Wei Fang argued that the enemy vanguard must be light and elite troops—if battle went well it would not be enough for merit, and if it went badly it would damp our army's momentum; as the Art of War says, wait at ease for the weary—better not to strike.

units.zh: 兵旣精強，城又險固，慶之攻未能拔。
units.en: Their troops were elite and the city formidable; Qingzhi could not break it at first.
units.literal: The troops were already elite and strong, and the city was also perilous and solid; Qingzhi attacked but could not take it.

units.zh: 直以時事未安，且資慶之之力用，外同內異，言多忌刻。
units.en: but the realm was not yet secure, so for the moment they still needed Qingzhi's sword—outward allies, inward enemies, their speech sharp with suspicion.
units.literal: only because the times were not yet settled did they for the moment rely on Qingzhi's strength and use—outwardly the same, inwardly different, their words full of jealousy and harshness.

units.zh: 慶之心知之，亦密爲其計。
units.en: Qingzhi saw through them and laid plans of his own in secret.
units.literal: Qingzhi knew it in his heart and also secretly made plans of his own.

units.zh: 顥欲從之，元延明說顥曰：「陳慶之兵不出數千，已自難制；
units.en: Hao was inclined to agree, but Yuan Yanming warned him, "Chen Qingzhi commands only a few thousand men, and they are already hard to control.
units.literal: Hao wished to follow this; Yuan Yanming urged Hao: "Chen Qingzhi's troops do not exceed several thousand, and already by themselves are hard to control;

units.zh: 慮慶之密啓，乃表高祖曰：「河北、河南一時已定，唯尒朱榮尚敢跋扈，臣與慶之自能擒討。
units.en: Fearing a secret report from Qingzhi, he wrote Emperor Wu: "Hebei and Henan are pacified for now. Only Erzhu Rong still struts defiantly—your servant and Qingzhi can deal with him ourselves.
units.literal: Fearing Qingzhi's secret memorial, he then memorialized the High Ancestor: "Hebei and Henan for the moment are all settled; only Erzhu Rong still dares to be overbearing and unruly—your servant and Qingzhi by ourselves can capture and subdue him.

units.zh: 洛下南人不出一萬，羌夷十倍，軍副馬佛念言於慶之曰：「功高不賞，震主身危，二事旣有，將軍豈得無慮？
units.en: Fewer than ten thousand southerners held Luoyang, while Qiang and other tribesmen outnumbered them tenfold. Vice commander Ma Fonian told Qingzhi, "Great merit goes unrewarded, and power that awes one's lord endangers the man who wields it. With both true, can you have no fears?
units.literal: Southerners in Luoyang did not reach ten thousand; Qiang and barbarians were ten times that number. Army Vice Commander Ma Fonian said to Qingzhi: "Merit high but unrewarded, shaking the ruler and peril to the person—these two things are already present; how can the general not have concerns?

units.zh: 慶之不敢復言。
units.en: Qingzhi said no more.
units.literal: Qingzhi did not dare speak again.

units.zh: 僧強頗知幻術，更相扇惑，衆至三萬，攻陷北徐州，濟陰太守楊起文棄城走，鐘離太守單希寶見害，使慶之討焉。
units.en: Seng Qiang knew sleight-of-hand and they whipped each other into frenzy until their host reached thirty thousand. They took Northern Xu. Jiyin administrator Yang Qiwen fled; Zhongli administrator Shan Xibao was killed. Qingzhi was ordered to suppress them.
units.literal: Seng Qiang was quite skilled in illusion arts and they fanned and deluded one another; the masses reached thirty thousand, attacked and took Northern Xu province, Administrator of Jiyin Yang Qiwen abandoned the city and fled, Administrator of Zhongli Shan Xibao was killed—the court sent Qingzhi to subdue them.

units.zh: 車駕幸白下，臨餞謂慶之曰：「江、淮兵勁，其鋒難當，卿可以策制之，不宜決戰。」
units.en: The emperor went to Baixia and, at the farewell feast, told Qingzhi, "Jiang and Huai fighters are fierce and hard to meet head-on. Use strategy, not a pitched battle."
units.literal: The imperial carriage went to Baixia; at the farewell feast he said to Qingzhi: "Jiang and Huai troops are strong; their edge is hard to meet—you may use stratagem to control them; it is not fitting to decide the matter in pitched battle."

units.zh: 慶之圍懸瓠，雄來赴其難，寶樂求單騎校戰，昕躍馬直趣寶樂，雄卽散潰，仍陷溱城。
units.en: While Qingzhi besieged Xuanhu, Xiong marched to relieve it. Baole asked for single combat. Xin spurred straight at him; Xiong's force broke and fled, and they took Qincheng.
units.literal: Qingzhi besieged Xuanhu; Xiong came to relieve the crisis; Baole requested single-horse trial combat; Xin leaped on his horse and charged straight at Baole; Xiong at once scattered in rout, and they still took Qincheng.

units.zh: 僧辯誅後，龕遣其將杜泰來攻長城，世祖拒之，命昭達總知城內兵事。
units.en: After Sengbian was killed, Kan sent Du Tai against Changcheng. Emperor Wen held the city and put Zhaoda in charge of the garrison.
units.literal: After Sengbian was executed Kan sent his general Du Tai to attack Changcheng; Emperor Wen resisted him and ordered Zhaoda to take overall charge of troops within the city.

units.zh: 及杜泰退走，因從世祖東進，軍吳興，以討杜龕。
units.en: When Du Tai withdrew, he followed Emperor Wen east. The army camped at Wuxing to attack Du Kan.
units.literal: When Du Tai withdrew, he followed Emperor Wen eastward; the army was at Wuxing to campaign against Du Kan.

units.zh: 侯景聞神茂敗，乃遣其中軍侯子鑒帥精兵二萬人，助神茂以擊嵊。
units.en: Hou Jing heard Shenmao was defeated and sent his central army Hou Zijian with twenty thousand crack troops to help Shenmao attack Sheng.
units.literal: Hou Jing heard Shenmao was defeated and sent his central army Hou Zijian with twenty thousand crack troops to help Shenmao attack Sheng.

units.zh: 三年，宮城陷，御史中丞沈浚違難東歸。
units.en: In the third year the palace city fell; censor-in-chief Shen Jun fled east in hardship.
units.literal: In the third year the palace city fell; censor-in-chief Shen Jun fled east in hardship.

units.zh: 粲還至廬陵，聞侯景作逆，便簡閱部下，得精卒五千，馬百匹，倍道赴援。
units.en: Can returned as far as Luling, heard Hou Jing had rebelled, reviewed his men, gathered five thousand picked troops and a hundred horses, and hurried to the rescue by forced marches.
units.literal: Can returned as far as Luling, heard that Hou Jing had rebelled, reviewed his subordinates, got five thousand picked troops and a hundred horses, and hurried by forced marches to the rescue.

units.zh: 武陵王舉兵至峽口，王琳偏將陸納等據湘州應之，沖為納所拘。
units.en: When the Prince of Wuling marched to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others seized Xiangzhou in support; Chong was held by Na.
units.literal: When the Prince of Wuling raised troops to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others held Xiangzhou in response; Chong was detained by Na.

units.zh: 梁世為國子周易生，射策舉高第，除祕書郎、太子舍人、宣惠武陵王主簿、輕車河東王功曹史。
units.en: Under Liang he studied the Book of Changes at the national university, took top marks in the archery-and-writing examination, and served as secretary, mentor to the heir apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and records officer to the Prince of Hedong.
units.literal: In Liang he was a National University student in the Book of Changes, scored highest in the archery-and-writing examination, appointed Secretary, Mentor to the Heir Apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and Records Officer to the Prince of Hedong.
